uncited: Gradient selection uses `hash & 15` to pick one of 12 gradient directions in 3D, mapping to x, y, or z with sign flips based on bits 0 and 1 [see [Perlin Noise 2D](4211-perlin-noise-2d.md)].
Fade function: $Fade(t) = t \cdot t \cdot t \cdot (t \cdot (t \cdot 6 - 15) + 10)$; smooth interpolation polynomial applied to fractional coordinates [see [Perlin Noise 2D](4211-perlin-noise-2d.md)].

Grad function: $Grad(hash, x, y, z)$: $h = hash \& 15$; $u = h < 8 ? x : y$; $v = h < 4 ? y : h == 12 || h == 14 ? x : z$; return $((h \& 1) == 0 ? u : -u) + ((h \& 2) == 0 ? v : -v)$; computes dot product of gradient vector and distance vector [see [Perlin Noise 2D](4211-perlin-noise-2d.md)].
